QF.id: Cat III AIF Due Diligence and Risk_14

question.text: To mitigate counterparty risk, a Cat III AIF should:

answer.text: Diversify across multiple prime brokers and counterparties; assess creditworthiness

explanation.text: The Logic: Counterparty risk in a Cat III AIF — the risk that a broker, prime broker, custodian, bank, NBFC, distributor or other counterparty fails to meet its obligations — is generally mitigated by (a) diversifying across multiple prime brokers and counterparties so no single failure is catastrophic, (b) actively assessing the creditworthiness and financial health of each counterparty before onboarding, and (c) periodically reviewing those counterparties to catch deteriorating credit quality. Using only one prime broker concentrates risk, ignoring counterparty exposure is plainly inadequate, and "only use offshore" does not address credit quality at all. The Trap: Single-counterparty or ignore approaches increase risk; offshoring per se does not lower counterparty credit risk. Note: The NISM Series XIX-B AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook pages checked define counterparty risk but do not state the specific mitigation steps (multiple prime brokers, creditworthiness assessment, annual prime-broker financial-health reviews); the framing above reflects general hedge-fund industry counterparty-risk management practice rather than a workbook citation.
